# Pitch

## Initial Context & Idea

Goal:  provide users shorter term 3-month subscription option (with introductory), increase conversion of first payment

Foundation : 
-  Our colleagues from MuseScore had successful experience with such flow, we would like to try it also
-  Previously, we had 1-year introductory offers that show good results but were not rolled out
-  We will provide a discount for the first 3-month period

### Questions & Answers

What is the main message to user?
A small amount looks less scary to user. Users will be more willing to make their first purchase and also see the benefit compared to a monthly subscription.

What are the prices / discounts?
Three variants:
1) $19.99 for the first 3-month intro-period, $34.99 for others
2) $24.99 for the first 3-month intro-period, $39.99 for others
3) $39.99 for the first 3-month intro period. $54.99 for others
can you please help with calculations
UPD. Since we rollout , the prices will be $19.99 for the 3-month plan, $24.99 for 6-month plan

What plans will be on paywall?
for 1st iteration:
Variant B: Year with trial, 3 months, month
Variant C: Year with trial, 6 months, month

What plan will be highlighted as a default?
In the cases, where we don't offer the trial, we can highlight new 3 month plan

## Confidence research

## Hypothesis

If we introduce a new a lower-priced three-month trial plan in the main subscription funnel,   we expect the conversion to payment to increase by 10-14% without a decrease in user retention, because we lower the financial entry barrier, making it easier for users to try the subscription

# Results

[macro]
true #7502
-

Exposure event: App Experiment Start

## Decision

Do not roll out. 

Var C (6-month plan) shows statistically significant harm: subscribers −11.1% (p=0.028), buyers −11.9% (p=0.038).

Var B (3-month plan) shows consistent negative trends across ARPU (−7.1%), CR to buyers (−9.0%), and revenue ($26,472 vs $28,987 control) without reaching significance but with no compensating upside.

The positive trial mechanics signal (+22–26% trial share, +22–26% trial→charge) does not offset the loss of instant annual subscription revenue — the two plans acted as substitutes, not additions.

### Next steps

Re-check churn and refund metrics in ~2 weeks once the 14d charge window matures (currently Pending 14d Charges: Var B 24.0%, Var C 15.7% — preliminary).

Investigate the anchor effect: test whether keeping the instant annual plan alongside the 3-month trial plan avoids the substitution effect and recovers conversion.

Review Instant Accesses drop (627 → 470 → 282) as a signal that the annual instant plan is a key conversion driver on web — consider protecting it in future paywall iterations.

## Significance analysis

Significant results (p < 0.05):

Trials share: Var B +22.7% (p&lt;0.001), Var C +12.2% (p=0.014)

Trial → charge: Var B +21.7% (p=0.006), Var C +25.8% (p=0.008)

CR members → subscribers: Var C −11.1% (p=0.028)

CR members → buyers: Var C −11.9% (p=0.038)

Not significant : ARPU, ARPPU, AOV, subscriptions per user, charges per user, churn 14d, refund 14d.

ARPU is negative in both variants (Var B −7.1%, Var C −10.8%) without reaching significance. CR to subscribers and buyers is negative, significantly so for Var C. Revenue in absolute terms: $28,987 (control) vs $26,472 (Var B) and $14,668 (Var C).

Trial mechanics improved strongly (+22–26% trial share, +21–26% trial→charge) while overall subscriber conversion fell. 

Refund 14d shows +33–40% in test variants, though not significant and pending maturity — worth re-checking once the 14d charge window closes

## Insights

[macro]
true Plans distribution over the variations
How the distribution of plans have changed over the variations?  

[macro]
sql SQL true 0, datetime) AS is_auth,
min(rt.datetime) as exp_start_datetime,
min(e.datetime_end) as exp_end_datetime
from default.ug_rt_events_web rt
left join exp_data e
on 1=1
where rt.date between '2026-05-27' and '2026-06-08'
and rt.event in ('App Experiment Start')
and has(rt.experiments.id, 7502)
and rt.item_id = 7502
and rt.unified_id <> 0
and rt.platform = 1
and rt.datetime between e.datetime_start and if(toDate(e.datetime_end) = '1970-01-01', toDateTime('2029-01-01'), e.datetime_end)
and cast(rt.rights % 10 as Int8) in (0, 4, 5)
group by 1, 2
)
, subscribed as (
select
e.variation,
s.subscription_id as subscription_id,
s.product_code as product_code,
s.product_id as product_id,
s.funnel_source as funnel_source,
s.funnel_start_action as funnel_start_action,
s.trial > 0 as trial,
toString(s.base_price) as base_price,
if(lower(funnel_source) like '%upsel%' or lower(funnel_source) like '%book%' or lower(funnel_source) like '%course%' or funnel_source = 'menu', 'upsell', 'other') as type,
max(s.unified_id) as unified_id,
min(s.datetime) as subscribed_dt,
min(s.date) as subscribed_date
from default.ug_subscriptions_events s
inner join exp_users e
on s.unified_id = e.unified_id
where s.date between '2026-05-20' and today()
and s.platform like '%WEB%'
and s.event = 'Subscribed'
and s.datetime between e.exp_start_datetime and if(toDate(e.exp_end_datetime) = '1970-01-01', toDateTime('2029-01-01'), e.exp_end_datetime)
and lower(s.funnel_source) not like '%email%'
group by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8
)
, charged as (
select
subscription_id,
product_code,
min(case
when product_id = 'com.ultimateguitar.tabs.one.intro.1year2' then 39.99
when product_id like '%.intro.%' and billing_cycle = 1 then usd_price * 0.5
else usd_price
end) as charged_revenue,
min(datetime) as charged_dt
from default.ug_subscriptions_events
where date >= '2026-05-20'
and platform like '%WEB%'
and event = 'Charged'
group by 1, 2
)
, refunded as (
select
subscription_id,
product_code,
min(case
when product_id = 'com.ultimateguitar.tabs.one.intro.1year2' then 39.99
when product_id like '%.intro.%' and billing_cycle = 1 then usd_price * 0.5
else usd_price
end) as refunded_revenue,
min(datetime) as refunded_dt
from default.ug_subscriptions_events
where date >= '2026-05-20'
and platform like '%WEB%'
and event = 'Refunded'
group by 1, 2
)
select
sub.variation as variation,
case
when (trial = 1 and type = 'upsell' and base_price = '99.99') or base_price = '99.99' then 'trial bundle upsell 99.99'
when (trial = 1 and type = 'upsell' and base_price = '59.99') or base_price = '59.99' then 'trial books/courses upsell 59.99'
when product_id like '%3_month%' then '3 month'
when product_id like '%6_month%' then '6 month'
when lower(funnel_start_action) like '%ambulance%' or lower(funnel_source) like '%ambulance%' or base_price = '19.99' then 'ambulance'
when lower(funnel_start_action) like '%comeback%' or lower(funnel_source) like '%comeback%' then 'comeback'
when trial = 1 and type = 'other' and base_price = '39.99' then 'trial'
when type = 'other' and base_price = '9.99' then 'month'
when trial = 0 and type = 'other' and base_price = '24.99' then 'instant'
when trial = 0 and type = 'other' and base_price = '29.99' then 'instant > 24h'
when trial = 0 and type = 'other' and base_price = '39.99' then 'instant ex-trial'
else 'other'
end as type_agg,
-- trial,
-- base_price,
uniqExact(sub.subscription_id || sub.product_code) as accesses,
uniqExactIf(sub.subscription_id || sub.product_code, sub.subscription_id = ch.subscription_id) as charges,
sumIf(ch.charged_revenue, sub.subscription_id = ch.subscription_id) as charged_revenue,
uniqExactIf(sub.subscription_id || sub.product_code, sub.subscription_id = r.subscription_id) as refunds,
sumIf(r.refunded_revenue, sub.subscription_id = r.subscription_id) as refunded_revenue
from subscribed as sub
left join charged as ch
on sub.subscription_id = ch.subscription_id
and sub.product_code = ch.product_code
left join refunded as r
on sub.subscription_id = r.subscription_id
and sub.product_code = r.product_code
group by 1, 2
order by 1, 2]]>
[/macro]

The hypothesis that cheaper short-term plans would shift users from trial to instant was not confirmed — the opposite occurred. Instant-type accesses fell from 21% to ~10%, while trials grew from 27% to 33–37%. The new 3- and 6-month plans captured only a portion of the lost instant volume; the remainder moved into trial or did not convert. This suggests the annual instant plan was not a price barrier but a preferred commitment format for high-intent users. Its removal reduced immediate-payment conversions rather than unlocking a new paying audience.
